source.quote: LUMIN's own page for the P1 Mini, read 2026-11-24. Network playback: « Up to DSD512 »; « Up to 384 kHz, 16-32-bit, Stereo ». Digital INPUTS: « USB » « DoP 128 support » / « PCM 44.1-384 kHz, 16 / 32-bit, Stereo »; « OPTICAL/SPDIF: » « PCM 44.1 kHz-192 kHz, 16-24-bit » / « DSD64 (DoP64, DSD over PCM) »; « HDMI: » « PCM 2.0 Audio support ». Digital outputs: USB « Native DSD512 support » / « PCM 44.1-384 kHz, 16-32-bit, Stereo »; BNC SPDIF « PCM 44.1 kHz-192 kHz, 16-24-bit » / « DSD64 (DoP64, DSD over PCM) ». Converter: « Dual ESS SABRE32 ES9028Pro DAC chips ». Processing: « DSD256 upsampling option for all files »; « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files »; « MQA QRONO d2a filters available for all PCM music (excluding via AirPlay) ». Footer and legal as on the X2 page; no prohibition.

facts.chip: « Dual ESS SABRE32 ES9028Pro DAC chips » - the ES9028Pro where the P2 has the ES9038Pro, every published figure otherwise identical.

device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

_les_filtres_MQA_QRONO_sont_nommes_et_co: « MQA QRONO d2a filters available for all PCM music (excluding via AirPlay) ». A NAMED filter - QRONO d2a - offered for all PCM, not only for MQA material, and withdrawn on one transport. No device_settings entry is written: the page never says how to select it or what it does to the signal, and a filter whose effect is undocumented cannot be recommended. It is the sixteenth filter name collected in two days and the first whose availability depends on which protocol the music arrived over.
_une_entree_AES_en_moins_que_le_P2: The P2 reads « AES/OPTICAL/SPDIF: » and this one « OPTICAL/SPDIF: » - the AES/EBU socket is what the larger model adds, and the figures for the sockets they share are identical. So the two records differ in a fitted input and in a chip generation, which is what makes them two devices rather than two editions.
